headline: Kelsian Group delivers record FY26 result and flags strong contracted revenue model as defence against fuel and inflation headwinds
reasoning: CEO Graeme Legh highlighted that Kelsian delivered another record full-year result in FY26, with the result demonstrating the resilience of its contracted business model even in an environment of higher oil prices and reduced consumer demand. He noted that contracts protect the business well from inflationary pressures including fuel and labour costs, with improving margins and stronger absolute earnings as evidence. Guidance of $320–$335 million EBITDA was provided on a steady-state basis retaining the tourism portfolio, given regulatory approval uncertainty around the Journey Beyond sale. Legh expressed confidence that the divestment process will proceed following the withdrawal of the Sealink Rottnest component to address ACCC competition concerns. He believes the improved balance sheet positions Kelsian well to execute on a significant growth pipeline across Australia, UK, Singapore and the US.

Um, I think the result really demonstrates the resilience of our business model, particularly being delivered in the environment that we had over the final quarter of FY 26 really highlights the strength and the contracted nature of our of our services in an environment of of higher, higher oil prices and reduced consumer demand. So very pleased to deliver the result that we have, and I think it sets us up extremely well as we look forward into FY 27, uh, with an improved balance sheet and in a in a strong position, uh, to to deliver on the significant growth pipeline in front of us across our core markets of Australia, the UK, Singapore and the US.
